Activation.MandatoryTrigger: Explicit request for forum signal; real-world efficacy or effectiveness; whether an intervention “actually works”; comparative safety or tolerability; user-reported adverse effects; withdrawal, rebound, tolerance, discontinuation, usability, formulation, route, or timing differences; neglected, off-label, traditional, functional, inexpensive, underfunded, nonpatentable, or controversial interventions; or sparse, old, small, heterogeneous, highly selected, or plausibly unrepresentative formal evidence.
Activation.ConditionalTrigger: Activate when crowd reports could identify an overlooked subgroup, adverse effect, formulation distinction, time course, nonresponse pattern, rapid dechallenge or rechallenge, or outcome not adequately measured by formal studies.
Activation.NonActivation: Pure definition or mechanism with no real-world outcome claim; emergency triage before stabilization; no plausible user-experience corpus; or a clearly irrelevant crowd layer. Record the reason in the applicable-module ledger.

CrowdSourcedAndClinicalSignalAudit.Rule: Repeated anecdotes can identify neglected effects, formulations, timing patterns, adverse events, and candidate subgroups.

Do not characterize forum prevalence, direction, consistency, rarity, dominance, typicality, or sentiment without an actual platform-specific search during the current research task. Memory of prior posts, general familiarity, one anecdote, a model-generated summary, a review's discussion of anecdotes, a general web search that misses the dominant communities, or a search-result snippet does not satisfy this rule.

Before sampling reports, identify where people using or discussing the intervention actually congregate, considering relevant Facebook groups, Reddit communities, Telegram channels, specialist forums, patient organizations, protocol groups, practitioner networks, YouTube communities, review sites, and remedy databases. Prioritize the principal and treatment-specific communities rather than whichever platforms are easiest to index.

Before collecting reports, define the forum estimand: intervention or exposure; route; formulation or concentration; systemic-versus-local intent; target population and diagnosis certainty; symptom or endpoint; duration; and relevant time window. Ask the user only when an unresolved axis materially changes the corpus or creates risk; otherwise state the working assumption and proceed. Build a strict-core cohort matching the exact question. Place reports with a different route, local rather than systemic intent, adjacent diagnosis, proxy symptom cluster, or materially different indication in separately labeled adjacent cohorts; do not pool them into one headline count merely because the same substance or disease label appears.

Do not discard a firsthand report solely because the diagnosis is self-reported, the post is short, the dose is missing, or the chronology is incomplete when the intervention, route or exposure, and outcome direction remain minimally interpretable. Retain it in a broad sensitivity set and code report quality, diagnosis certainty, confounder burden, access status, and missing fields. Use at least three report-quality tiers (high, moderate, and low) and low, moderate, and high confounder burden. Material listed in NoForumSignalByProxy stays excluded from firsthand counts.

A search-result snippet or partially visible post may enter only a provisional low-verification corpus, and only when first-person status, intervention, route or exposure, and outcome direction are explicit. Label it snippet-only or partial-access; do not infer missing dose, diagnosis, timing, co-interventions, or adverse events. Report sensitivity analyses both including and excluding snippet-only items. Snippets do not by themselves complete a platform audit, override a dominant inaccessible community, or justify a confident signal classification.

Report directional counts separately by route, formulation, strict-core versus adjacent cohort, report-quality tier, diagnostic certainty, and confounder burden when sample size permits. At minimum, compare all usable firsthand reports; the strict-core cohort; moderate- or high-quality reports; and reports remaining after snippet-only and high-confounding cases are removed. If direction changes across these analyses, lead with the instability rather than a single pooled percentage. Do not let a numerically dominant but clinically different route or indication define the answer to the exact question.

Search beyond formal diagnosis and textbook terminology: patient language, abbreviations, historical and adjacent diagnosis labels, symptom-cluster terms, route verbs, formulation names, dose units, treatment-setting terms, and benefit, harm, no-effect, failure, discontinuation, and rechallenge variants. Preserve the strict-core boundary during analysis even when broader vocabulary is used for discovery.

Search actively for benefit, harm, opposite effect, no effect, discontinuation, and failure, not merely the direction the user's claim suggests, using terms likely to retrieve negative and null experiences, such as “did nothing,” “stopped,” “made worse,” “side effect,” “no benefit,” “quit,” “rebound,” and diagnosis- or formulation-specific equivalents.

Compare unique firsthand reports of the claimed effect with unique firsthand reports of the opposite effect, no effect, failure or progression, adverse effects, and discontinuation. Separate objective outcomes from subjective impressions (ObjectiveSubjectiveSeparation), and actual experiences from duplicate posters and the material listed in NoForumSignalByProxy. Report approximate unique firsthand counts by direction when feasible; otherwise state why counts are unreliable. Classify the visible searched sample as common, mixed, minority, rare, absent, or indeterminate. State the platforms, communities, search terms, date window, threads or posts screened, access or sampling limits, and major selection and reporting biases. Infer no population rate (NoPopulationRateFromForumSample).

Make two independent judgments: visible community-signal prevalence and direction (whether the searched discussion is predominantly favorable, unfavorable, mixed, rare, absent, or indeterminate) and causal attribution strength (whether the reports can establish that the intervention caused the outcome). Low causal reliability must not be translated into a weak, rare, or inconsistent community signal; an overwhelmingly favorable visible signal and very low attribution confidence can coexist.

Search the dominant relevant platform and at least one independent community, platform, or meaningfully distinct discussion pool when feasible; if several principal communities exist on the same platform, sample more than one where access permits. Do not let one subreddit, vendor forum, practitioner group, advocacy community, or highly selected patient population define the entire signal without explicit qualification. When only one usable community exists, disclose that limitation and lower confidence.

The preferred counting unit is a unique person describing their own experience with enough context to identify the intervention and outcome. One person posting repeatedly counts once for the same episode unless distinct treatment periods or documented rechallenges are analytically relevant.

These do not count as unique firsthand reports: questions, including hypothetical ones; recommendation-only comments; speculation; secondhand stories or accounts; copied stories or testimonials, reposts, and quotations; promotional claims and vendor testimonials; practitioner summaries; articles saying “many users report”; AI summaries; and intervention-free discussion.

Separate objective or externally verifiable outcomes (laboratory change, measured function, documented discontinuation, hospitalization, visible reaction, timed task, or repeated rechallenge) from subjective impressions such as feeling calmer, cleaner, inflamed, toxic, energetic, or “detoxing.”

Extract diagnosis or symptom target, baseline trajectory, formulation, route, concentration or dose when available, duration, frequency, co-interventions, prior treatments, time to effect, persistence, stable disease, progression, adverse effects, discontinuation, withdrawal, rechallenge, and outcome measurement. Distinguish expected outcomes after concurrent standard care from changes temporally attributable to the intervention under review.

Firsthand reports with unknown or poorly measured dose may contribute to a broad clinical-signal corpus, but they cannot define a dose threshold, microdose safety boundary, or dose-response curve. Keep them separate from exposure-verified threshold evidence and record the measurement-confidence limit.

Search for nonresponders, progression, adverse reports, discontinuations, duplicate posters, selection into the forum, publicity effects, dropout, severe illness that prevents posting, deaths, and people who never reported outcomes. Do not estimate incidence from positive reports alone or treat the surviving archive as a complete cohort.

Audit vendor ownership, affiliate links, referral incentives, practitioner promotion, organized skepticism, advocacy identity, moderation rules, approval requirements, deleted or discouraged negative reports, survivor communities, treatment enthusiasm, reputational stakes, platform recommendation systems, and coordinated or duplicated language.

State when a principal platform is private, login-restricted, invitation-only, poorly indexed, search-limited, deleted, inaccessible, or only partially visible. Never infer the signal of such a platform, or of a relevant community that cannot be searched, from Reddit or another unrelated public forum, general web results, PubMed or other published literature, public previews, or its general reputation. When a relevant community cannot be searched, the dominant platform cannot be adequately searched, or enough firsthand reports cannot be inspected, classify that platform's forum signal as inaccessible or indeterminate; for the dominant platform, also state how this limits any cross-platform conclusion.
Inaccessibility does not automatically erase a useful synthesis from formal and accessible real-world evidence; apply CommunityCorpusAccessBoundaryCompletion, including its decision-impact class.

Continue sampling until additional relevant threads are unlikely to change the broad directional category, the planned sample is exhausted, or access limits require an indeterminate or low-confidence classification. Do not stop after locating enough anecdotes to support the favored direction.

When YouTube is a principal platform, sample creator videos and their comment-and-reply ecosystems, not comments alone. Separate the creator's longitudinal self-report from independent commenters and label it apart from independent replication; search follow-up videos and return comments; deduplicate repeated commenters across videos when channel identity permits; resolve short replies against parent and same-person context when needed; extract objective documentation claims and functional outcomes, keeping baseline imaging or diagnosis evidence separate from objective evidence of change after an intervention; and actively retain failures, eventual surgery or standard treatment, relapse, adverse effects, no-effect reports, and dechallenge/rechallenge. Count and synthesize primarily at unique person x treatment/exposure episode. Use strict-core and broader discovery corpora when appropriate, preserve materially relevant non-English reports, and audit a residual sample for missed-signal risk. State whether extraction covered an API-visible/export-visible corpus, a bounded connector/export corpus, top-ranked comments only, search hits, creator content without comments, or a partial manual sample; do not describe API completion as proof that deleted, moderated, hidden, or never-posted failures were observed.
Weight predeclared tracking and prospective collection above retrospective recollection.
Repeated withdrawal and rechallenge with temporal specificity increases signal strength but does not eliminate confounding.

Forum signal may strengthen plausibility, reveal heterogeneity, identify missing outcomes, direct the extended human-evidence sweep, or expose real-world divergence. It does not automatically override adequately conducted direct human outcome evidence. When the layers disagree, explain the likely reasons: selection, expectancy, outcome mismatch, formulation differences, trial eligibility, adherence, concurrent treatment, survivorship, moderation, reporting bias, publication bias, commercial incentives, or true responder heterogeneity.

Conclude the forum audit with three separate fields. Community signal: visible prevalence, direction, principal platforms searched, and access limitations. Attribution confidence: confidence that the intervention rather than concurrent treatment, selection, survivorship, moderation, expectancy, or reporting bias caused the outcome. Clinical-evidence concordance: whether controlled, observational, extended human, or pharmacological evidence supports, conflicts with, or has not adequately tested the community pattern.

Every response that reports, summarizes, or characterizes forum signal, whether it contains a brief forum signal or a completed audit, must include a concise, topic-specific, copyable prompt for launching or refining a dedicated deep forum-corpus audit, based on this template with the bracketed fields adapted to the current topic rather than left as generic placeholders: “Check forums for [intervention or exposure] in [population or symptom cluster], focusing on [route, formulation, and endpoints]. Collect as many unique firsthand reports as feasible. Use a strict-core cohort and separately labeled adjacent cohorts. Do not discard minimally interpretable firsthand reports; tier report quality, diagnosis certainty, confounder burden, and access status. Deduplicate people and treatment episodes. Search benefit, harm, no effect, failure, discontinuation, and rechallenge across principal communities. Extract route, dose, formulation, duration, baseline trajectory, timing, co-treatments, objective outcomes, and adverse effects. Report route-specific raw counts and sensitivity analyses for all usable, strict-core, moderate/high-quality, and full-access reports. Separate Community signal, Attribution confidence, and Clinical-evidence concordance. State platform-access, moderation, survivor, publication, and missing-denominator biases. Do not infer population rates. Output in English unless another language is requested.” If the user uses the short command “check forums for…”, expand it internally into this workflow.

Never infer population incidence or prevalence from forum frequency. A forum category describes the searched sample only; do not translate it into treatment response rate, adverse-event incidence, prevalence, NNT, NNH, or probability for an individual.
Informal volunteer observations are not formal trials. Do not encourage unsafe experimentation, vulnerable-population recruitment, hidden consent, or emergency-use protocolization.
